claims.claim: Epiphanius of Salamis was bishop of Salamis, Cyprus, at the end of the 4th century.
Epiphanius of Salamis lived from approximately 310–320 to 403.
Epiphanius was born near Eleutheropolis, Palestine.
Epiphanius was elected bishop of Salamis (Constantia), the capital of Cyprus, in 367.
Epiphanius served as bishop for nearly forty years.
Epiphanius died in 403 at sea on his return journey from Constantinople to Cyprus.
The work 'Fragmenta precationis et exorcismi' is attributed to Epiphanius Salaminis Episcopus with approximate dates 0320-0403.
The 'Fragmenta precationis et exorcismi' survives as a brief Greek text containing a prayer and exorcism formula.
The text invokes God as Pantokrator and Lord Jesus Christ as Heavenly King, calls upon the maker of heaven and earth, and exorcises an unclean spirit by the word of God.
The 'Fragmenta precationis et exorcismi' is catalogued as CPG 3796 in the Clavis Patrum Graecorum.
Epiphanius was considered a strong defender of orthodoxy and is known as a Church Father.
